description: Targeted improvements: expand resume about field beyond VARCHAR 255, add month/year date picker for experience dates, enrich admin dashboard with live previews, translate public site to Brazilian Portuguese, and restyle tech stack section to be minimal/subtle.

userStories.title: Expand `about` field to TEXT in backend
userStories.description: As an admin, I want to write a long resume bio without hitting a character limit so that I can fully describe my background.
acceptanceCriteria: ResumeEntity.about is annotated with @Column(columnDefinition = "TEXT") so the database column stores unlimited text
The corresponding DTO and mapper pass the value through unchanged (no truncation)
Existing data is preserved after the schema change
mvn test passes
userStories.notes: Added @Column(columnDefinition = "TEXT") to ResumeEntity.about. DTO and mapper pass value through unchanged.

userStories.title: Month/Year date picker for experience dates
userStories.description: As an admin, I want to pick a month and year for each experience's start and end dates using a date picker so that I don't have to type and remember the YYYY-MM format manually.
acceptanceCriteria: Start Date and End Date inputs in the experience form are changed from type="text" to type="month"
When saving, the frontend converts YYYY-MM to YYYY-MM-01 before sending to the backend API
When loading existing data, the frontend converts YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM to pre-populate the month picker
The End Date field has a 'Presente' checkbox; when checked, endDate is sent as null and the input is hidden/disabled
The picker respects dark mode styling consistent with other form inputs
pnpm tsc --noEmit passes
userStories.notes: Changed type="text" to type="month" for start/end date inputs. Added toMonthInput/fromMonthInput utilities. Added Presente checkbox that sends null endDate.

userStories.title: Rich content preview on admin dashboard
userStories.description: As an admin, I want to see a live preview of key content fields on the dashboard so that I can quickly verify what is currently published without navigating away.
acceptanceCriteria: The dashboard fetches about, resume, and posts data on page load (reusing existing adminApi.ts calls)
About card shows: name, current title/role, and the first ~100 characters of the bio (truncated with ellipsis)
Resume card shows: full name, number of experiences, and the most recent experience company name + date range
Posts card shows: total post count, and the titles of the 3 most recent posts
A loading skeleton or spinner is shown while data is being fetched
If a fetch fails, the card falls back gracefully showing the description text and a subtle error indicator (no crash)
pnpm tsc --noEmit passes
userStories.notes: Dashboard converted to client component. Fetches about/resume/posts in parallel with Promise.allSettled. Shows skeletons while loading, live previews after, error badge on failure.

userStories.title: Translate public site to Brazilian Portuguese
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want to read the portfolio in Brazilian Portuguese so that the content feels native and professional.
acceptanceCriteria: Every hardcoded English string visible to public visitors is replaced with Brazilian Portuguese
Dynamic content (fetched from backend API) is untouched — only hardcoded UI strings are translated
Dates displayed publicly use pt-BR locale formatting (e.g. jan. 2022 - jun. 2024)
pnpm tsc --noEmit passes
userStories.notes: Updated Header, Footer, TechStack, utils.ts (pt-BR locale + Presente), curriculum, content, content/[id], and home page. Direct string replacement, no i18n framework.

userStories.title: Restyle tech stack section to be a subtle, minimal detail
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the tech stack section to feel like a quiet detail rather than a prominent UI element so that it complements the page without competing with the main content.
acceptanceCriteria: The tech stack section occupies noticeably less vertical space than before
Tech icons are rendered in grayscale/low-opacity by default
Item borders are removed or made near-invisible
If a React Bits component is used, it is installed via the @react-bits registry and integrated correctly
The section looks intentional and polished, not broken or empty
pnpm tsc --noEmit passes
